messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the late-night incident — repeated p99 latency spikes on /generate. Going to capture action owners and a temporary SLO plan here.

alex: Numbers?

maria: p95 ~140ms -> 320ms, p99 ~480ms -> 1.1s for ~18m window. Throughput steady. Traces point to KV cache churn.

prashant: Confirmed. A canary experiment changed cache behavior for long prompts; saw KV miss bursts.

maria: Proposed actions: 1) revert canary cache change for canary cohort (owner: prashant, target: tonight deploy). 2) Add KV hit/miss ratio and endpoint p99 panels to the main SLO dashboard (owner: alex, target: 48h). 3) Short-term SLO policy: allow /generate p99 <=900ms for 7 days from revert, with error-budget burn threshold 20% (owner: tara, target: 2024-05-09). 4) Add an automated detector for "p99 > 2x baseline for 15m" that creates a high-priority incident (owner: maria, target: 2024-05-06).

tara: I'll draft precise SLO language and include rollback criteria: if p99 > 850ms for any 30m sliding window post-revert, escalate back to postmortem.

alex: For dashboards I'll surface miss ratio with PromQL: sum(rate(redwood_inference_kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_inference_kv_request_total[5m])) and add request-size distribution.

prashant: Revert plan: revert flag to canary, deploy, observe 6h; if p99 improves to <700ms we promote. I'll also tag canary requests with TTL variant to prove causality.

maria: I'll open a follow-up ticket with checklist: revert PR, canary instrumentation, dashboard panels, temp SLO doc, synth monitors per region, 24h observation window.

sre-bot: Incident 2024-04-30-2312: state updated to "followup-in-progress" and owners assigned (prashant, alex, tara).

maria: We'll review status at tomorrow's handoff and in SLO governance sync. Thanks all.
